claim: The installed Redstone carries examples/ in its package directory (URL or registry); route 2 (temp env, Pkg.develop of both paths) works; Pkg makes installed dirs read-only; developing the examples alone leaves Redstone unreachable
why: Probe probe.jl:56 found an installed package file at mode 100444, so Pkg makes it read-only. Developing examples/ alone (probe.jl:62-66): Redstone is in the manifest, but the direct deps are only ["RedstoneExamples"] and Base.identify_package("Redstone") returns nothing, so Redstone is unreachable. Route 2, developing both packages (probe.jl:68-70): both identify. examples/ is tracked, and no .gitattributes export-ignore drops it, so a URL or registry install carries it.

why: Probe line '021 build counts': y_state, y_direct, x_deriv, s_update, guard, handler and x_projection each ran exactly once during build. ws_init (2) and m_init/x_init/s_init (several) are declaration bodies outside §9.3's set.

why: src/build.jl:767-806: build runs the structure step, `_nominal`, and activation at each scalar in `activations`. Other activations derive lazily from the Build (src/build.jl:969), as the spec's next paragraph and §9.4 say. The build docstring says the same.

claim: If any unanchored component exists, deployment must declare Δt_base
why: src/deployment.jl:253-258: Δt_base = :derive with an unanchored discrete component is refused as DeploymentInvalid :unanchored, carrying `grid` (the constructive message). Probe: MultiRate :derive -> (:Δt_base, :unanchored), grid carried, paths fcs/inner, fcs/outer. The default path (Δt_base = Δt_frame) is accepted. | 'Must declare Δt_base' means derivation is refused, as the bullet list above it says (derivation only with A₀ unpopulated). D-283 used the same wording beside a non-keyword default source. A clearer wording: 'deployment must not derive `Δt_base`; it takes the keyword or `Δt_frame`'.

claim: the §13.8 tracer activation follows the rule identically, a whole-model run at the tracer scalar like any activation
why: src/build.jl:969-974 and 1030-1041 run any scalar through the same _activate with the same _frozen gating; probe: activation(build(FreeGain()), Redstone.Tracer{true}) returns an Activation{Tracer{true}} | Nothing in src/ requests the tracer activation; src/tracer.jl:7-8 says it is not built there. The rule holds for it whenever it is requested.

why: test/test_build.jl:2260-2300 (build_dual_sweep builds every zero-argument component with activations=(Float64, ProbeDual), one Dual activation per component)

claim: the payload carries the field-level diff (missing / unexpected / per-field expected-vs-observed)
why: src/diagnostics.jl:1114-1118 (observed/declared per field, observed_fields/declared_fields for the key set); probe: observed_fields=[:a,:z], declared_fields=[:a,:b] | Missing and unexpected are carried as the two field lists, not as separate computed sets.

Every loop call site calls rhs with no index: src/model.jl:619 and 632, src/trim.jl:602 and 744. rhs has no gated entries (build.jl:1545 pushes `nothing` gates), so its two chunk tuples share one type (probe P4: 'same tuple types: true'). | `rhs(tick)` is still a legal call. PhaseBody{I,I}(tick) (executor.jl:578) ignores the index and walks the interior, and test_executor.jl:21 and 141-143 pin that, so the roster is total in both arities. No index ever reaches rhs semantically. If the sentence is read as 'rhs accepts no argument', the code is broader than the spec.
